item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00275","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C05","C24"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.84,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 plausibly supplied a material rhetorical and structural template for the child. Both Eisenhower letters proceed from the goal of preserving peace, explain that modern weapons and long-range delivery create a continuing threat, characterize preparedness as both a deterrent and a means of responding if attack occurs, call for continuing modernization rather than reactions to changing international tension, and reject defensive arrangements so burdensome or regimented that they undermine the way of life being defended. C05 is a strong secondary candidate for the child's administrative discussion of federal civil-defense leadership, interagency participation, State and local consultation, and legislative recommendations. C24 supplies concrete machinery expressly used in the child—the Civil Defense Coordinating Board and integration of departmental civil-defense responsibilities—but its narrower operative framework appears less influential on the child's overall drafting than C04.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"An effective civil defense is an important deterrent against attack on our country and thus helps preserve peace. In the event of an attack upon us, civil defense at once becomes one of our immediate reactions imperatively required for our nation's survival.","parent_excerpt":"All these capabilities have a double value--they serve our aim in peacetime of preventing war through their deterrent effect; they form the foundation of effective defense if aggressors should strike.","explanation":"Both use the same two-part formulation: defensive capability deters war in peacetime and becomes essential protection if deterrence fails."},{"child_excerpt":"This need arises not from any increase in international tensions but, rather, from the recent spectacular developments in weapons and methods of delivery.","parent_excerpt":"The threat of modern war calls for constant modernization... characterized by a stability that is not materially disturbed by every propaganda effort of unfriendly nations.","explanation":"Both distinguish long-term modernization driven by weapons technology from short-term reactions to fluctuations in international tension."},{"child_excerpt":"One extreme would be to hold our people subject to a rigid discipline... But this approach, continued, would destroy the America we are determined to preserve.","parent_excerpt":"They must be adequate for this purpose but must not become such an intolerable burden as to occasion loss of civilian morale or the individual initiative on which, in a free country, depends the dynamic industrial effort which is the continuing foundation of our nation's security.","explanation":"Both balance preparedness against measures that would regiment citizens or damage the free society being defended."},{"child_excerpt":"The Federal Government, despite its increased civil defense role, must remain in partnership with States, cities and towns.","parent_excerpt":"the Board will undoubtedly find it necessary and advisable to call upon the other agencies of the Government and to consult with representatives of the States and local governments","explanation":"C05 provides a closely related administrative model of federal civil-defense leadership combined with interagency and State-local participation."},{"child_excerpt":"I will appreciate having your recommendations and those of the Civil Defense Coordinating Board","parent_excerpt":"To make recommendations to the President regarding specific arrangements involving the assumption of certain civil-defense responsibilities by the various departments and agencies.","explanation":"C24 supplies the exact coordinating institution and recommendation mechanism invoked in the child."}]}
